transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a little trouble staying focused lately. I mean, I'm sure everyone gets distracted sometimes, right? But for me, the main thing is I just seem to get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be trying to sit down and work on a job application, and then a car goes by outside, or my phone lights up, or I just get some random idea in my head. And then it just sends me somewhere else completely before I even notice I stopped working. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things right and giving you what you need.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and distractibility since you were a child, or is this a more recent development in your life?

Um, well, I guess it's actually been going on for a pretty long time. Like, since I was a little kid. I hope it's okay to go that far back? 

But, um, even in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my seat around. I think I was just... I don't know, a really eager kid? So I'd talk out of turn a lot without meaning to. And, um, I'd forget my homework sometimes, or I'd try to get through my worksheets really fast and end up making these silly, careless mistakes. I wasn't trying to be a bad student or anything, I promise, I just had a lot of energy and wanted to get things done. 

Does... does that answer your question okay? I can try to remember more recent stuff if that's better.
Do you find that you currently have a hard time staying seated or feeling restless when you are in situations where you are expected to be still, like in meetings or while watching a movie?

Um, yeah, I guess I do get a little antsy sometimes. I really don't want to sound like I don't know how to behave myself, I swear! It's just... well, I used to be really active. But since I can't play soccer like before, um, just sitting around the house makes me feel kind of... well, almost like I’m crawling out of my skin? 

I try to just relax and sit still, I really do, but I usually end up just pacing from room to room to let the energy out. 

I hope that doesn't sound too weird or bad? I just have a lot of pent-up energy, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers before a question is finished or interrupting others while they are speaking?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes? I mean, I really try to be a good listener, I promise. I don't want to be rude or anything. But sometimes, especially when I'm talking to my mom or, um, the counselor I see sometimes... an answer just kind of pops into my head. And before I even realize it, I've already said it out loud before they're completely finished talking. 

It's not that I'm trying to cut them off! It's just like my brain gets so excited that I know the answer, and it just slips out. I always feel really bad about it afterwards. 

Is... is that okay to admit? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad person. I really am working on being better about waiting my turn to speak.

When you have tasks that require sustained mental effort, like organizing your belongings or finishing a project, do you find that you frequently struggle to keep things in order or follow through to the end?

Um, well, I guess organization is... maybe a little tricky for me sometimes? I really try to stay on top of things, I promise. I want to be responsible. But, like, if I have a whole list of things I need to get done... um, like if I need to call my counselor, and also clean up my room, and maybe work on sending in a job application... it just gets a little overwhelming? 

I don't want to sound lazy, because I really do try! It's just that I look at everything and I'm not really sure which one is the most important to start with. So I'll, um, kind of start cleaning my room, but then remember the application, so I'll go look at that for a few minutes... and then I'll think about the phone call. So I end up kind of bouncing around between all of them, and I guess I just end up half-finishing everything instead of getting one thing totally done. 

I really am trying to get better at making lists and stuff to fix it. Does... does that make sense? I hope that's an okay answer.

Looking at the last six months, would you say that your struggles with staying focused and organized are more prominent than your struggles with feeling restless and interrupting others, or do you feel that both types of issues are equally present?

Um, well... I guess I'd say they're both kind of there about the same amount? I mean, I really don't want it to sound like my life is totally chaotic or anything, I promise. I try really hard to keep everything under control. 

But yeah, if I'm being totally honest, I think the trouble with keeping things organized and the... the pacing around and blurting things out... they both happen pretty regularly. Like, I'll be bouncing between tasks because I can't figure out where to start, and then later that same day I'll be pacing the house because I just have all this extra energy I don't know what to do with. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just totally out of control. I really am trying my best to manage both sides of it. Is... is it normal for both of those things to be happening at the same time like that?
